source_inspection_notes: Read assembly.py in full: flags any node with `NodeType.ASSEMBLY` in any function DECLARED in the contract being analyzed (`f.contract_declarer != contract: continue` skips inherited-but-not-redeclared functions). This is a genuine mere-PRESENCE check with no safety/protection judgment baked in -- the cleanest trigger/scope match found in this batch. Run across every contract in the compiled project (not just one), it should catch assembly usage wherever it's actually declared, including in library/parent contracts analyzed as their own compilation-unit members.

derivation_trace.analyzer_behavior: Flags every function-declaring contract's own ASSEMBLY-type nodes, unconditionally on any safety judgment.
covered_cases: all directly-declared assembly usage in the compiled project
uncovered_cases: the Set-of-Overriding-Requirements exception (req-2-safe-assembly / req-2-documented / three named compiler-bug overrides / one external v1-predecessor reference) -- this detector fires unconditionally on presence, so like req-1-compiler-060, it cannot by itself determine whether an override applies, capping this at PARTIAL_MATCH rather than EXACT_MATCH despite otherwise clean trigger/scope equivalence
derivation_trace.final_classification: PARTIAL_MATCH -- the cleanest trigger/scope fit in this batch, held back from EXACT_MATCH purely by the override-outcome issue common to nearly every requirement in this Set-of-Overriding-Requirements family, not by any detector imprecision.
